alternative_uses(k1).text: Owners can move covered units to uses the ceiling does not reach.

binding(k1).text: The ceiling binds: it is below the price the market would otherwise reach.

buyer_substitutes(k2).text: Legal substitutes are acceptable to some buyers.

buyers_organize(k2).text: The buyers have a concentrated stake and can organize for repeal.

buyouts_limited(k1).text: Buyouts move fewer tenants than the cap keeps in place.

can_organize(k1).text: The groups with a concentrated stake can organize and spend to keep or change the rule.

can_organize(k2).text: The former legal sellers can organize to seek repeal.

commutable(k1).text: Shut-out buyers can buy in a neighbouring market outside the rule's reach at a bearable cost.

counterfactual_catches_up(k1).text: Without the rule, the market price soon passes any raise made in the announcement window.

demand_persists(k2).text: A meaningful share of buyers keep wanting the good after the ban.

durable_assets(k1).text: The covered assets are durable and their supply expands slowly.

enforced(k1).text: The ceiling is enforced against most bound sellers.

enforced(k2).text: The legal sellers comply with the ban.

enforcement_risk(k2).text: Informal sellers face a real risk of punishment.

evasion(k1).text: Some exchanges take place above the ceiling without being caught.

evasion(k2).text: Enforcement is imperfect: many informal sales go undetected.

exit_process(k1).text: Moving covered units to an alternative use requires a permit or board process.

expected_to_last(k1).text: Buyers of the covered assets expect the rule to last for many years.

keepers_dominate(k1).text: Among all protected tenants, the fall in moves out of the area among keepers outweighs the rise among the displaced.

lockin_dominates(k1).text: The lock-in outweighs moves diverted out of the area by higher free rents.

no_other_use(k2).text: The legal sellers cannot replace the banned good with other products for most of their business.

nontransferable(k1).text: The protected buyers' right is tied to holding the tenancy and cannot be sold.

opportunities_need_move(k1).text: Some valued opportunities for the protected buyers would require giving up the covered unit.

quality_adjustable(k1).text: Sellers have room to cut quality or maintenance above any enforced minimum.

relet_obstructs(k1).text: Re-letting a vacated unit obstructs the owner's later move to an alternative use.

search_open(k1).text: Seekers find covered units by their own search: no public list or allocation rule assigns them.

selection_open(k1).text: Sellers may choose among applicants by criteria of their own.

substitutes(k1).text: Uncovered units in the same market are close substitutes for covered ones.

window_repricing(k1).text: Enough contracts come up for repricing in the announcement window, and sellers can raise the price on them.

would_leave(k1).text: Without the rule some protected buyers would have left the area.

source_sentences: Resale cap: no person who resells or offers to resell a ticket to an event held in Selvar, and no platform that lists or processes payment for a resale, may resell above face value plus 10%.
Face value is the price charged by the primary seller, including taxes and the primary seller's own fees, as printed or recorded by the primary seller.
The Act asserts jurisdiction over any resale of a ticket to an event in Selvar, wherever the parties or platform are.
Resale by registered charities at auction is exempt.
The bill was introduced on 3 February 2027, signed on 12 May 2027, and applies to resales made on or after 1 September 2027.
The civil penalty is up to $500 per ticket resold above the cap.
No new appropriation is made: the division absorbs the work within its existing $14 million budget.
Bot ban: software that evades a primary seller's purchase limits or access controls is prohibited, for any person who uses or sells it.
The civil penalty is $2,500 per ticket obtained with it.

Existing rules, in force without the Act too: primary sellers' terms forbid bots and purchase limits, and tickets bought in breach may be cancelled, enforced by the seller alone; a primary seller may make tickets non-transferable or limit resale to its own exchange; consumer protection law prohibits fake tickets and speculative listings of tickets not held, enforced by the same division.

context: About 9.5 million tickets a year are sold for events in Selvar. About 11% (1.05 million) are resold. Of those, about 52% (545,000) are resold above face value plus 10%, at a median markup of 70% and several times face value for the most sought-after events; the rest are resold at less, many below face value, mostly for events that do not sell out.
The State of Brackmere, whose capital Brackmere City is 55 minutes from Dunholt, has a 14,000-seat arena and no resale law; about 40% of the arena tours that play Dunholt also play Brackmere City.
